newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Labour protests erupted across the country after Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea on Thursday announced that 17 state-run factories would be shut to speed up restructuring of industry. Thirty thousands jobs will be lost.
Energy, raw materials, water and transport services are being cut to all 17 plants.
* More than 5,000 oil workers from the Vega and Petrotel oil refineries -- on Ciorbea's restructuring list -- massed in central Ploiesti and demanded talks with government representatives.

A Ploiesti union leader said oil workers expected other unionists to join the protest. He said people were especially upset by the fact that a third of the planned job cuts will affect the Prahova county, where Ploiesti is located.
Three of the 17 companies -- the oil refineries of Petrotel and Vega and the Romfosfochim chemical plant -- are in Prahova.

* Some 5,000 employees of Romfosfochim -- located in Valea Calugareasca, in the outskirts of Ploiesti -- have blocked the main railway linking Bucharest to Romania's eastern region of Moldova after their company was put on the restructuring list.
* Several hundred employees at the Darmanesti oil refinery in Bacau gathered in the courtyard to protest against its planned closure. Power was still on and the refinery was operating normally.
* Lignite mining trade unions announced they cancelled a two-hour strike after the government met their demands.
